title: Today in one sentence
text: Before the open, the main question is whether Monday's tech bounce (QQQ up 1.2%, Amazon up 5.0%) carries on after last week's drop, with Lockheed Martin's results on Thursday and the Fed meeting on October 27 and 28 still ahead.

title: Chip stocks still below their highs
text: Nvidia, Broadcom, Taiwan Semiconductor and AMD each rose between 1.4% and 1.8% on Monday. Even so, Broadcom sits about 32% below its 52 week high and AMD about 18% below. A bounce is one good day, not a new trend, so watch whether the buying continues at the open.

title: Lockheed Martin reports on Thursday
text: Lockheed Martin will share its quarterly results before the market opens on Thursday, October 22, with a call at 8:30 a.m. Eastern. On report days a stock can move a lot, up or down, because real numbers replace guesses.

title: Interest rates are still the big worry
text: The Federal Reserve meets October 27 and 28, and recent inflation news was hotter than analysts expected. Reports disagree on how likely another rate hike is. The monthly average 10 year Treasury yield was 4.99% in September, the highest in our 12 month chart.

title: Calmer areas slipped on Monday
text: Eli Lilly fell 1.3%, GE Aerospace 0.8% and Lockheed Martin 0.7%, while utilities on the Nasdaq dropped 3.4%. When money rushes into tech, quieter areas can lag for a day.

title: Lesson 14: What is inflation?
text: Inflation means prices slowly rise over time, so the same dollar buys a little less each year. If a snack costs $1.00 today and prices rise 3% in a year, it costs $1.03 next year. Governments measure it with a report called the Consumer Price Index, or CPI. When inflation is higher than expected, the Federal Reserve may raise interest rates to cool things down, and that is why stock markets watch these reports so closely. It also shows why saving money in a place that earns nothing can lose buying power. This is for learning, not advice to buy or sell anything.
